role: ARM Serial Wire Debug on STM32F030F4P6TR (SWDIO=PA13, SWCLK=PA14) to a 5-position 0.1 inch through-hole header J2 for a flying-lead ST-LINK / J-Link / DAPLink class probe. 2-layer, bench-only, 3.3 V logic.
_verdict: SWD binds NOTHING on this board: no controlled impedance, no differential pair, no length matching, no series termination, no return-path rule, and ZERO added components. The empty high_speed and diff_pairs lists below are a deliberate engineering result, not an omission - see the research doc sections 3 and 10 for the arithmetic and for what would overturn it.
notes: NET NAMES SWDIO / SWCLK / NRST / +3V3 / GND are proposals in the standard's conventional form. The architect reconciles them at P2 (local-label nets will carry a leading slash: /SWDIO, /SWCLK, /NRST; +3V3 and GND stay bare); netlist_audit verifies at P4. None of them matches check_diffpair's auto-discovery suffixes (_P/_N, DP/DM, D+/D-), so no pair is discovered by accident.

high_speed IS DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Fastest edge the STM32F030 can produce on any GPIO is tr = tf = 5 ns max (DS DocID024849 Rev 3 Table 48, OSPEEDR=11, CL=30 pF, VDD >= 2.7 V), and that is also the REAL default for SWDIO: RM0360 Rev 5 section 8.4.3 gives GPIOA_OSPEEDR reset value 0x0C00 0000, i.e. bits 27:26 = 11 = High speed on PA13 (PA14 is left at Low speed, moot since the MCU never drives SWCLK). Reflections on an unterminated 40 mm FR-4 trace settle in about 1.5 ns; the SWD sampling instant is a half-bit away - 125 ns at ST-LINK/V2's 4 MHz, 20.8 ns at STLINK-V3's 24 MHz. Margin 14x to 80x. Declaring these nets would add check_return_path findings that are unfixable by construction on a 2-layer board (LEARNINGS.md 2026-07-30 [check_return_path][stackup]: 'declaring a net can only ever raise the finding count'), for a risk that does not exist. This repo's own shipped STM32 board agrees: stm32-blinky's constraints.json declares only /OSC_IN and /OSC_OUT in high_speed, not its SWD nets.

diff_pairs IS AN EXPLICIT EMPTY LIST AND THAT HAS SEMANTICS. constraints_schema.md: an explicit empty list DISABLES check_diffpair board-wide; omitting the key lets it auto-discover by name suffix. SWD is single-ended - it has no pair - and bb-mcu has no differential pair anywhere, so both readings are no-ops here (and stm32-blinky shipped 'diff_pairs': []). The architect should still merge this consciously rather than by copy-paste.

NO CONTROLLED IMPEDANCE IS EVEN PURCHASABLE. reference/stackups.yaml JLC2313_1.6 carries controlled_impedance: [] with the provenance note that JLC's getImpedanceTemplateSettingList returns 0 templates for stencilLayer=2 (live-verified 2026-08-06). A 50 ohm single-ended target on that stack would need a ~2.7 mm trace. Never emit impedance_ohm for this interface on a 2-layer board.

BOM: NO PULL-UP AND NO PULL-DOWN. What ARM actually requires (IHI 0031G, ADIv5, section B4.3.2 'Line pull-up', p. B4-122): 'To make sure that the line is in a known state when neither host nor target is driving the line, a 100K pull-up is required at the target.' TWO PRECISIONS: (a) that requirement is on SWDIO ONLY - ADIv5 states NO SWCLK pull-down requirement anywhere (a SWCLK pull-down is a vendor recommendation: SEGGER 'recommended', Lauterbach 1k-47k with 10k typical); (b) 100K is ARM's value and the STM32's internal pull is STRONGER, not weaker - 25/40/55 kohm (DS Table 46), sinking ~82 uA when the probe drives SWDIO low versus ~33 uA at 100 k, negligible for any probe driver, and stronger is the safe direction. ST then draws the conclusion for this exact family, AN4325 Rev 2 section 4.3.3: 'The reset states of the GPIO control registers put the I/Os in the equivalent states: SWDIO: alternate function pull-up; SWCLK: alternate function pull-down. Having embedded pull-up and pull-down resistors removes the need to add external resistors.' (AN4488 section 6.3.3 repeats it for the F4 family.) Corroborated by DS Table 11 note 7 and RM0360 Rev 5 GPIOA_PUPDR reset 0x2400 0000.

KNOW THIS BEFORE A REVIEWER RAISES IT - ST CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE SWDIO PULL-UP. RM0360 Rev 5 section 26.5.1 says 'For SWDIO bidirectional management, the line must be pulled-up on the board (100 kohm recommended by Arm)', which reads like a board requirement. RM0360 section 26.3.3 and AN4325 section 4.3.3 are ST's explicit counter-statement: the on-die ~40 kohm pull-up on PA13 satisfies it. That resolution holds ONLY while PA13 stays a dedicated debug pin - which requirements.md section 2 guarantees on this board. If a later phase repurposes PA13, this reopens.

BOM: NO SERIES TERMINATION on SWDIO or SWCLK - a CONSIDERED REJECTION of real vendor recommendations, not an absence of guidance. ARM's ADIv5 requires nothing and ST is silent (checked across AN4989, AN4325, AN4488, AN5967, RM0360, UM2448), but THREE PROBE VENDORS DO RECOMMEND ONE: Raspberry Pi RP-003139-SP specifies 100 ohm source termination at both ends 'very close to the IC pins' and calls the target-side pair 'not strictly required but highly recommended unless the platform is very low cost and/or space constrained'; Lauterbach recommends 47 ohm 'near the processor' on SWDIO/SWO - explicitly NOT on SWCLK; SEGGER sells a 47 ohm signal-smoothing adapter. Note NO vendor source exists for the commonly-cited 22R or 33R, and they only ever go on the target-DRIVEN line (SWDIO), never SWCLK. Rejected here on RPi's own three rationales taken in turn: reflections settle in ~1.5 ns against a 125 ns half-bit (nothing to damp); EMC slew limiting is moot because requirements.md section 4 runs no EMC campaign; and short-circuit/ESD current limiting is PROTECTION, the first class block-only excludes by mode - so per build-modes.md it is never a reviewer finding. Do NOT defend this with 'no source asks for it' - they do.

BOM: NRST NEEDS NOTHING ADDED. Internal pull-up is permanent, 25/40/55 kohm (DS Table 49). Internal glitch filter already rejects pulses up to V_F(NRST) = 100 ns and guarantees reset at V_NF(NRST) >= 300 ns for 2.7 V < VDD < 3.6 V (DS Table 49). Probes drive reset open-drain (Hitex, 'Selecting a debug header for Arm Cortex-M devices'), so open-drain plus the internal pull-up is a complete reset circuit.

BOM: NO 0.1 uF NRST CAPACITOR - SETTLED BY ST'S OWN BOM SPLIT, not left open. DS Figure 21 p66 'Recommended NRST pin protection' shows 0.1 uF (value confirmed by rendering the figure, not by text extraction; its '(3)' superscript has no matching note text in Rev 3 or Rev 5 - an ST doc defect). AN4325 Rev 2 then files it under Table 6 OPTIONAL components, described as 'Capacitor C4 100 nF 1 Ceramic capacitor for RESET button' - and bb-mcu has NO reset button by mode. Its stated job (protection against parasitic resets) is a class block-only excludes, and the die already carries a filter that rejects everything up to 100 ns. stm32-blinky fit one (C9 100 nF) but that is not a binding precedent against a vendor 'optional'. If the architect keeps it anyway, keep it at 0.1 uF - a larger value slows the probe's reset edge.

NRST ON THE HEADER IS THE RIGHT CALL AND ST SAYS SO. AN4325 Rev 2 section 6.1.4: 'It is recommended to connect the reset pin in order to be able to reset the application from the tool.' AN4325 Figure 7 'SWD port connection' shows the connector carrying NRST, SWCLK, SWDIO, VDD and GND - the SAME FIVE SIGNALS the owner fixed for J2, so the owner's pin set is the vendor's own reference connection. AN4989 Rev 4 section 4.2.1: 'ConnectUnderReset: Debugger takes control while asserted NRST pin ... This is required in case of a reconnection to a system in Low-Power mode or which has changed SWD pin to alternate functions.' Without NRST the tools silently fall back to a software system reset (AN4989 section 4.2.5), which cannot recover a part whose firmware already released the SWD pins - the cost this repo already recorded on stm32-blinky: 'with no NRST at the header, connect-under-reset is unavailable ... any future firmware that remaps PA13/PA14 or stops the core can brick-until-boot0-bodge.' bb-mcu has no reset button by mode, so NRST on J2 is the board's only reset control and only recovery path.

THE 3V3 PIN IS A SENSE INPUT, NOT A RAIL - ST AND SEGGER BOTH STATE THE DIRECTION. UM2448 Rev 9 Table 6 describes STDC14 pin 3 T_VCC as 'Input for STLINK-V3SET'. SEGGER UM08001 section 13.5: 'VTref is the target reference voltage. It is used by the J-Link to check if the target has power, to create the logic-level reference for the input comparators and to control the output logic levels to the target. It is normally fed from Vdd of the target board and MUST NOT HAVE A SERIES RESISTOR.' So wire it straight to +3V3 - which is what the owner ruled - and put nothing in series. Probes refuse to connect if it reads 0 V. NAMING: ST never calls it VTREF on its own connectors - it is T_VCC or VDD_TARGET; reconcile silk and schematic labels accordingly. CURRENT DRAWN (now sourced, no longer assumed): J-Link BASE/PLUS '< 25 uA', J-Link EDU Mini '< 170 uA'; ST publishes no ST-LINK figure. Worst sourced case 170 uA = 0.17 % of this board's < 100 mA budget, so no power[] entry is warranted - but the power architect should know the rail has one more consumer. Pre-hardware-v9.2 J-Links powered their level shifters off VTref (mA class) and would draw more, still trivially inside budget.

BACK-POWERING: NO PROBE CAN BACK-POWER THIS BOARD THROUGH J2 - now answered per probe, not reasoned. STLINK-V3: UM2448 section 1 Note, 'The STLINK-V3SET product does not provide power supply to the target application.' J-Link: SEGGER, 'VTref is only a voltage reference used by the probe to determine the target's logic level. It is not intended to power the target system' - J-Link's target supply is on 20-pin PIN 19 ONLY (5 V, max 300 mA, off by default via the Power command; KS/Kickstart models ship with it ON). ST-LINK/V2: pins 1/2 VAPP = 'Target VCC', an input; its 20-pin pin 19 reads 'VDD (3.3 V)' in ST's table but the target-connection column says 'Not connected'. ST-LINK/V2-1 (Nucleo CN4): VDD_TARGET = 'VDD from application', no power output on the debug connector. RPi Debug Probe / DAPLink: 3-pin SC/GND/SD, no VTref pin and no power pin at all. THE SINGLE REAL HAZARD IS PIN 19 OF A 20-PIN HEADER, AND J2 DOES NOT HAVE ONE. The bench rule in requirements.md section 3 (power from J1 only) still stands for procedure hygiene and for the reversed-plug case below - but not because of a documented back-drive path.

P6 SILK - THIS IS THE ONE THAT GETS FORGOTTEN. J2 is an unkeyed 0.1 inch header, so per-pin silk is the ONLY thing preventing a reversed plug. ARM's own connector solves this with a shroud and a blocked KEY pin (pin 7); a bare header has neither. stm32-blinky PROMISED silk-labelled pins in its architecture and SHIPPED WITHOUT THEM - review-board.md WARNING 1 also records that its lone pin-1 square pad is covered by the header body after assembly. Label all five pins, place the text outside the connector body footprint, and add a pin-1 marker that survives assembly.

PIN ORDER PROPOSAL (the owner fixed the SET and gave the ORDER to the layout engineer): use 3V3 / SWCLK / GND / SWDIO / NRST. This is ST's own STLINK-V3SET CN6 flying-lead order with SWO dropped (UM2448 Rev 9 Table 11: 1 T_VCC, 2 T_SWCLK, 3 GND, 4 T_SWDIO, 5 T_NRST, 6 T_SWO), which is also the Nucleo CN4/CN3 order - so anyone wiring from ST's published pinout gets it right by reading straight down. It is also the SAFE order: on a 5-position header a 180-degree reversal maps position i to position 6-i, so position 3 maps to itself, and with GND on the centre pin a reversed plug shorts nothing. By contrast the order as listed in requirements.md (3V3 / SWDIO / SWCLK / NRST / GND) reversed puts 3V3 onto the probe's GND wire - a hard short of the 3.3 V rail into a 0.5 A bench supply, exactly the failure this repo's reviewer flagged on the shipped board: 'ST-Link clones are wired pin-by-pin; swapping 3V3/GND shorts the debugger's 3.3 V rail to ground' (stm32-blinky review-board.md WARNING 1). The proposed order additionally puts ground between the two debug signals, as ARM's 10-pin connector does (pin 3 GND beside pin 4 SWDCLK).

P6 PLACEMENT FACT, NOT A CONSTRAINT: on the TSSOP-20 (DS Figure 8) SWDIO is pin 19 and SWCLK is pin 20 - adjacent at one corner - and VSS/VDD are pins 15/16 on the same side, but NRST is pin 4 on the OPPOSITE side of the package. J2 cannot take all four signals off one face; NRST has to come around or under. Worth weighing when the architect sets placement.edges for J2, which this fragment deliberately does not do.

LAYOUT GUIDANCE (advisory, not enforced). Keep J2 close to the MCU - Lauterbach: 'A direct and short connection (no buffer or level shifter) between the probe connector and the processor is recommended'; Hitex: 'worth trying to keep the connector relatively close to the micro to maintain good signal integrity'. NO VENDOR GIVES A TRACE-LENGTH NUMBER and none gives a maximum cable length either (nearest quantitative statement anywhere: RPi's 'over a few 10s of CM of cable and PCB ~30MHz performance should still be achievable', and that is WITH their 100 ohm terminations). ASSUMED <= 50 mm on SWDIO/SWCLK, inside the strictest critical length with margin. Run the debug traces over the B.Cu ground pour where convenient - good practice, but NOT declared in high_speed on purpose. Keep SWCLK clean: Lauterbach, 'The debug interfaces are not fault tolerant. A spike on the TCK/TMSC/SWCLK clock will most likely cause communication to fail, requiring a re-initialization of the debug interface and a restart of the debug session.' The real transmission line is the probe's unshielded flying lead, which no layout choice can improve - and SEGGER notes 'long ground leads can significantly worsen ringing and distortion', which is the board's half of the problem (see the pin-order note). A twisted ground wire for flying leads is folklore - no vendor documents it.

CHECKED NEGATIVE: ST PUBLISHES NO SWD-SPECIFIC LAYOUT RULE ANYWHERE - verified absent across AN4989 Rev 4, AN4325 Rev 2 section 5, AN4488 Rev 7 section 8, AN5967 Rev 5 section 14, RM0360 and UM2448. Their high-speed routing sections cover SDMMC, FMC, QuadSPI/XSPI and ETM only. TRAP FOR LATER PHASES: do NOT cite AN5967 section 14.4.5's 'Trace impedance: 50 ohm +/- 10%. All the data traces must be as short as possible (<= 25 mm)' as an SWD rule - that is the ETM PARALLEL TRACE PORT (TRACECLK + D[0:3], near HCLK/2), not SWD. Applying it here would import a controlled-impedance requirement this interface does not have, onto a 2-layer stackup that cannot deliver it.

SPEED FACTS AND A CHECKED NEGATIVE: the STM32F030 datasheet contains NO JTAG/SWD AC characteristics table at all (the only serial-interface AC table in section 6.3 is Table 58, SPI), and ST states no 'SWCLK < N x HCLK' ratio rule anywhere - AN4989 section 4.2.1's only prerequisite is that FCLK/HCLK be enabled and the GPIO clocked. The binding number is the probe's, and ST recommends the top of it: AN4989 Rev 4 section 5.2, 'On system with a core clock greater than 1 MHz, it is safe to use the highest 4 MHz SWD speed'. Probe ceilings, from vendor spec text: ST-LINK/V2 and V2-1 'up to 4 MHz (default: 1.8 MHz)' (UM1075 Rev 9 Features); STLINK-V3 'up to 24 MHz' (UM2448); J-Link BASE/PLUS 15 MHz and J-Link EDU Mini 4 MHz (SEGGER spec tables); CMSIS-DAP/DAPLink default 1 MHz with no specified maximum (DAP_DEFAULT_SWJ_CLOCK), RPi Debug Probe docs using 5 MHz. 4 MHz is the realistic bench maximum - it is the hard ceiling of the two probes people actually own - and the verdict above holds at 24 MHz too.

WHAT WOULD OVERTURN THIS FRAGMENT: a probe clocking SWCLK above ~50 MHz (none exists in this class), adding SWO trace output to J2 (excluded - the owner fixed a 5-pin header with no SWO), or a board large enough that SWDIO/SWCLK exceed ~80 mm of trace. None is in play. Re-open only if one becomes true.
